sections.heading: The Roof, the Gutters and the Adjuster in One Call
body: A storm goes through, or a stain shows up on the ceiling, and you're suddenly managing three things at once: the roof, the gutters that took the same beating, and an insurance company you'd rather not argue with.
Most people end up playing messenger between a roofer, a gutter crew and an adjuster. We'd rather you didn't.
Roof replacement, roof repair and gutters are all one job here, and so is the insurance side. We look at the roof, explain what we find, and work with your insurance company when there's a claim.

Stacia does a lot of that work: the first look at the roof, the adjuster's visit, the paperwork after. You call one company for the roof, the gutters and the claim, instead of relaying messages between three.

sections.quote: Diamond Roof & Gutter was the best choice for replacing my roof. They are a full service roofing company. From examining the damaged roof to working directly with my insurance adjuster to the installation of the new roof and guttering I couldn't have been in better hands.
sections.name: Margaret W.

sections.heading: When Insurance Is Part of Your Roof
body: The adjuster comes once, walks around, takes photos and leaves. A letter follows. If you've never been through a roof claim, it's hard to know whether what you were offered matches what's on your roof.
That's the gap a roofer can fill. We spend our days on roofs, so we know what storm damage looks like and what a replacement really involves.

We meet the adjuster at your roof and go through the paperwork with you afterward. Stacia has stood next to a lot of adjusters, and she knows the difference between damage that was missed and damage that isn't there.
Whether to file is your decision, and what gets paid is your insurance company's. We can't promise an outcome, and nobody honest can.
What we can do is make sure the person deciding has seen your whole roof.

sections.quote: Stacia was the most professional contractor I have worked with in a very long time. … Problems with the insurance company would not have been settled were it not for her calm, knowledge, and experience!
sections.name: Michael H.

sections.heading: Roof Replacement
body: Some roofs are finished. Shingles curl or crack across several slopes, bare patches show, granules pile up at the bottom of the downspouts, or the leaks have moved from one spot to two.
At that point a patch only buys you a season. A replacement is the honest fix, and it's the job we do most.
We help you choose the brand and color, so the new roof suits the house and the street. If your gutters are worn or damaged, we replace them in the same job.

sections.heading: Roof Repair
body: Shingles in the yard after a windy night, or a leak that only shows up in heavy rain, doesn't always mean a new roof. Sometimes it's a few shingles, a cracked pipe boot or flashing that has let go.
We look first and tell you straight whether a repair will hold or whether you're paying to patch a roof that's past it.

sections.heading: Gutters and Downspouts
body: Gutters get ignored until they overflow at the edge of the roof, sag away from the house or dump water next to the foundation.
Water that doesn't leave the roof edge soaks the fascia behind it and the soil under it. Gutters that pull away usually mean the fasteners or the board behind them have given out.
We install gutters, repair them and fix drainage problems. When a roof is being replaced, doing the gutters in the same job means one crew, one cleanup and a matching edge along the whole house.

sections.quote: We had an excellent experience with Diamond Roof and Gutter. Stacia supported us through the entire experience from her initial review of our roof, engaging with the insurance company and leading us through the process every step of the way including a gorgeous roof, new gutters and additional work on the home.

sections.heading: A Crew That Leaves the Yard Clean
body: Roofing throws off nails, torn shingles and debris, and most of it lands in your yard and driveway.
We clean up at the end of every work day, not only at the end of the job. It matters most with kids, pets and tires.

sections.heading: Homes, Rentals and Home Sales
body: Not every roof is on the house you live in. We've worked on homeowners' own roofs, on rental and investment properties, and on roofs that had to be done during a home sale.

A rental needs a roof done quickly and without drama. A sale needs it finished cleanly so nothing slips in the transaction. In both cases you need a straight answer about the roof and a crew that finishes cleanly, so you can get back to the tenant or the closing.

sections.heading: Is It Time for a New Roof?
body: A roof wears out a little at a time. By the time it leaks, the damage underneath has usually been going on for a while.

The signs are on the surface. Shingles curl at the edges or crack, bare patches show where the granules have worn off, and the gutters fill with grit from the shingles. Leaks that were one spot become two.
A roof that has been patched several times, or that took hail or wind damage across more than one slope, is usually past repairing. Patching a worn roof only buys you a season.
Not every leak means a new roof, though. If the damage is in one place and the rest is sound, we'll say so and point you to [roof repair](/roof-repair-wichita-ks/).

sections.heading: After a Storm: the Adjuster and the Paperwork
body: Storm damage turns a roofing job into an insurance job. Someone has to document what happened, meet the adjuster and keep the paperwork moving.

We do that part with you. We look at the roof first, come out when your adjuster does, and go through the paperwork afterward. Stacia has walked a lot of homeowners through this, so you aren't learning the process alone.
We can't say what your insurance company will pay. We can make sure the whole roof has been looked at, and that you aren't explaining roofing to an adjuster by yourself.

sections.heading: Choosing the Brand and the Color
body: The shingle you pick decides how the house looks for the next couple of decades, and it's easy to get lost between brands, lines and colors.
A few things narrow it down. Darker colors show off a roofline but run hotter in a Kansas summer.
Heavier architectural shingles cost more than basic ones and tend to wear better. Your neighbors' roofs and your siding matter too.
We walk you through the options and help you land on one that fits your house and your budget, so you aren't choosing from a sample board alone.

sections.heading: A Roof During a Home Sale, or on a Rental
body: A failing roof can stall a sale. A buyer's inspector flags it, and the roof becomes the thing everyone is waiting on.
We've replaced roofs while a house was being sold, and on rental properties where the owner wants the job done and the tenants left alone. In both cases the job has to be finished, clean and on time.

sections.heading: Roof and Gutters in One Job
body: Your gutters hang off the edge of the roof you're replacing. New roof edge, old gutters is how you end up paying a second crew to come back.
If your gutters are worn, bent or pulling away, we replace them while we're there. You get one crew, one schedule and one cleanup, and the roofline looks finished instead of mismatched.

sections.quote: Diamond Roof and Gutter did a great job on our new roof and gutters. … They treated our property as it was their own by cleaning up all trash and nails at the end of each work day.

sections.heading: Weather and Your Schedule
body: Roofing depends on the sky. Rain and high wind stop the work, and a roof that's torn off has to be dried in before the weather turns.
Size, pitch and what the crew finds under the old shingles also change how long a roof takes. That's why we don't promise a day count before we've been on your roof.
Our job is to keep you informed. When the schedule moves, you hear it from us. And when you're up against a deadline, tell us on the first call.

sections.heading: Shingles Missing After the Wind
body: You come home after a windy night and there are shingles in the yard, or a bare patch shows from the street. A missing shingle exposes the layer underneath, and that layer was never meant to face rain and sun.
Wind gets under the edge of a shingle whose seal has aged and lifts it. Once one goes, the ones beside it are easier to lift.
A repair here is usually small, and it's worth doing before the next storm. We replace what blew off and check the shingles around it.

sections.heading: A Leak Isn't Always Where the Stain Is
body: Water doesn't drip where it gets in. It enters at one spot, runs along the decking or a rafter, and shows up on your ceiling six feet away.
That's why a patch above the stain so often fails. The usual culprits are flashing around chimneys, vents and walls, cracked pipe boots, and valleys where two slopes meet.
A bead of caulk can hide bad flashing for a season. It doesn't fix it. A real repair finds where the water gets in and fixes that.

sections.heading: An Honest Look First
body: A repair estimate is where most people brace for the upsell: a small fix that turns into a full roof.
We'd rather you trust the estimate. You get an inspection and a price for what the roof needs, and if the answer is a repair, that's the job we quote.

sections.quote: Mike came out to do an inspection. He was on time, communicated well and gave me a great estimate. He walked us through what he saw and didn't try and upsell.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace?
body: A repair makes sense when the damage is in one place and the rest of the roof is sound.
Replacement makes sense when the trouble is everywhere: shingles curling across several slopes, grit in the gutters, leaks in more than one spot, or a roof that has been patched and keeps leaking.
We'll tell you which one you have. If it's a replacement, we'll say so plainly and explain why, and you can read how that job goes on our [roof replacement](/roof-replacement-wichita-ks/) page.

sections.quote: Diamond Roofing was honest and up front about repairing our roof and gutters. Their prompt response was so appreciated!

sections.heading: When Time Matters
body: A roof that's leaking right now can't wait for the next available week. Water that gets in keeps soaking insulation and drywall until someone stops it.
Call us and say it's actively leaking. If a storm caused it, an insurance claim may be part of the repair, and we work with your insurance company on it while the roof gets fixed.

sections.quote: Stacia is quick to respond and check a roof when time is of the essence and gives an honest evaluation. She works diligently with the client and insurance company to ensure the process moves along smoothly.

sections.heading: Gutters That Overflow, Sag or Pull Away
body: Gutter trouble often looks like a roof problem. Water spills over the edge during a storm, or the gutter hangs loose from the house.

We repair gutters, fix drainage problems and replace gutters that can't be saved. A gutter that sags is usually pulling on its fasteners or the board behind it, so fixing the real cause matters more than hanging it back up.

sections.heading: Repairs on Rentals and Investment Properties
body: If you own rentals, a leak is a tenant call and a lost evening. You need it fixed and you need to be told what happened.
We repair roofs on rental and investment properties as well as on homes, and when a roof is beyond repair we'll tell you so.

sections.quote: We've had nothing but very good experiences with Diamond Roof and Gutter in the last year, both on our own home as well as several investment properties. … All of the staff involved in our repairs and replacements were hard working and prompt.

sections.heading: What to Do While You Wait
body: Until someone can get to the roof, a few steps limit the damage:
list: Put a bucket under the drip and move furniture and rugs out of the way.
Take photos of the ceiling, the shingles in the yard, and any damage you can see from the ground. They help if there's a claim.
Stay off a wet roof. A fall is a bigger problem than a leak.

sections.heading: When to Call
body: Call as soon as you notice a leak or missing shingles. A lifted shingle or a cracked pipe boot is a small fix this week and wet decking a few storms from now.

footer.about: Diamond Roof & Gutter is a Wichita roofing company at 801 E Douglas. We replace and repair roofs, install and repair gutters, and work with your insurance adjuster.
why: Roofs and gutters in one job
Your Google reviews already make your case: 5.0 stars, with customers naming Stacia and her crews for the roof, the gutters and the insurance adjuster.

Your website works against all of that. Every phone number and Call button on it dials (781) 739-2688, a Massachusetts number. Your Google profile and the directories list (316) 640-6056, so a homeowner who taps Call on your site never reaches you.
The site was also returning errors when we checked: the plain address failed three times, and only the www address loaded.
So we built this site around the work your reviews describe, and every Call button dials the Wichita number.
